To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we developed a codon-optimization cloning protocol to construct a synthetic gene for the C-termini of human apoptotic protein GADD34, and expressed and purified the protein in large quantity.

we developed a novel protocol to assemble 19 oligonucleotidesto construct the synthetic GADD34 533-632 gene, cloned the gene into the E. coli expression plasmid pET28a(+), and produced and purified the recombinant GADD34 5-33-632 protein in large quantity.
we developed a codon-optimization protocol for cloning and expressing the C-termini of GADD34 and other proteins that are difficult to clone and express in E. coli.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an efficient and robust protocol for the production of a large quantity of the C- terminus of GADD34534-632.
the cloning, expression and characterization of a synthetic gene that codes for the GADD34 C-terminus, a protein that is known to be involved in apoptosis and DNA-damage.
the cloning, expression and purification of a novel apoptosis-associated protein, GADD34 C-terminus.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the synthetic GADD34 C-terminal fragment is an ideal model protein to study the structure-function relationship between HSV-1 g34.5 protein and its homologs.

the synthetic gene approach is an effective way for the production of proteins that are difficult to express in prokaryotes.
